intended_object: Given a class P of morphisms in the opposite category Cᵒᵖ, this is the corresponding class of morphisms in C: a morphism f : X ⟶ Y in C belongs to it exactly when f.op : op Y ⟶ op X belongs to P. This comes from the docstring and the name, by analogy with `MorphismProperty.op`.
explanation: The body is `fun _ _ f => P f.op`. It is exactly the standard way of moving a class of morphisms from Cᵒᵖ back to C: f is in `P.unop` if and only if f.op is in P. The only assumption is `CategoryStruct C`. That is the same setting in which `MorphismProperty` itself is defined, so the definition is already at its natural generality. It is the counterpart of `MorphismProperty.op`, and the two are inverse to each other. Nothing about degenerate cases is missing.
